section_1.title: The Setup: A Curious Experiment
section_1.content: Introduce the physical scenario: A frictionless surface, a wall on the left, and two blocks. A small block sits still, and a much larger block comes charging in from the right. We count every single collision (Block vs. Block and Block vs. Wall).
section_1.example: Imagine a giant Elephant-shaped block (Mass M) sliding toward a tiny Ant-shaped block (Mass m). If M = m, there are 3 collisions. If M = 100m, there are 31. If M = 10,000m, there are 314. The digits of Pi appear magically.

section_2.title: Prerequisite Knowledge: The Laws of the Game
section_2.content: Explain the two fundamental physics principles governing these collisions: Conservation of Energy (the system doesn't lose 'juice') and Conservation of Momentum (the 'push' is transferred). Visualize these as two mathematical equations that must always be satisfied.
section_2.example: Use an animation of a pulsing battery icon for 'Energy' and a directional arrow for 'Momentum' to show how they transfer between the Elephant and the Ant during a hit.

section_3.title: Mapping to Phase Space: The Velocity Vector
section_3.content: Instead of watching the blocks move in space, we plot their velocities on a graph. Let the x-axis be the velocity of the big block (v1) and the y-axis be the velocity of the small block (v2). Every state of the system is just a single point on this graph.
section_3.example: Show a 2D coordinate system where the 'state' point moves every time a collision occurs. A wall hit flips the y-coordinate; a block hit moves the point along a specific path.

section_4.title: The Geometry of Energy: Stretching the Circle
section_4.content: Explain that because Conservation of Energy (1/2 Mv1² + 1/2 mv2² = Constant) looks like the equation of an ellipse, we can 'rescale' the axes by the square root of the masses to turn that ellipse into a perfect circle.
section_4.example: An animation showing a squashed oval (ellipse) being physically stretched vertically until it becomes a perfect, glowing circle. The 'state' of our blocks is now a point trapped on the rim of this circle.

section_5.title: The Secret Angle: Why Pi?
section_5.content: Each collision corresponds to a 'jump' along the arc of this circle. Because of the mass ratio, each jump covers a tiny, constant angle. We count how many jumps it takes to go halfway around the circle (180 degrees or Pi radians) before the blocks move away from each other forever.
section_5.example: Visualize the circle as a clock face. Each collision is a 'tick' of the hand. As the mass of the Elephant increases, the 'tick' becomes smaller, requiring more hits to traverse the Pi-arc of the circle.

section_6.title: Conclusion: The Final Tally
section_6.content: Summarize how the number of collisions is the integer part of (Pi / angle). As the mass ratio becomes a power of 100, the angle becomes perfectly aligned with the decimal positions of Pi.
section_6.example: A final high-speed montage: M = 1,000,000m. The counter blurs as the blocks vibrate, finally stopping at exactly 3,141. The screen overlays the digits of Pi over the block counter.

section_1.title: The Setup: A Curious Experiment
section_1.content: Introduce the physical scenario: A frictionless surface, a wall on the left, and two blocks. A small block sits still, and a much larger block comes charging in from the right. We count every single collision (Block vs. Block and Block vs. Wall).
section_1.example: Imagine a giant Elephant-shaped block (Mass M) sliding toward a tiny Ant-shaped block (Mass m). If M = m, there are 3 collisions. If M = 100m, there are 31. If M = 10,000m, there are 314. The digits of Pi appear magically.

section_2.title: Prerequisite Knowledge: The Laws of the Game
section_2.content: Explain the two fundamental physics principles governing these collisions: Conservation of Energy (the system doesn't lose 'juice') and Conservation of Momentum (the 'push' is transferred). Visualize these as two mathematical equations that must always be satisfied.
section_2.example: Use an animation of a pulsing battery icon for 'Energy' and a directional arrow for 'Momentum' to show how they transfer between the Elephant and the Ant during a hit.

section_3.title: Mapping to Phase Space: The Velocity Vector
section_3.content: Instead of watching the blocks move in space, we plot their velocities on a graph. Let the x-axis be the velocity of the big block (v1) and the y-axis be the velocity of the small block (v2). Every state of the system is just a single point on this graph.
section_3.example: Show a 2D coordinate system where the 'state' point moves every time a collision occurs. A wall hit flips the y-coordinate; a block hit moves the point along a specific path.

section_4.title: The Geometry of Energy: Stretching the Circle
section_4.content: Explain that because Conservation of Energy (1/2 Mv1² + 1/2 mv2² = Constant) looks like the equation of an ellipse, we can 'rescale' the axes by the square root of the masses to turn that ellipse into a perfect circle.
section_4.example: An animation showing a squashed oval (ellipse) being physically stretched vertically until it becomes a perfect, glowing circle. The 'state' of our blocks is now a point trapped on the rim of this circle.

section_5.title: The Secret Angle: Why Pi?
section_5.content: Each collision corresponds to a 'jump' along the arc of this circle. Because of the mass ratio, each jump covers a tiny, constant angle. We count how many jumps it takes to go halfway around the circle (180 degrees or Pi radians) before the blocks move away from each other forever.
section_5.example: Visualize the circle as a clock face. Each collision is a 'tick' of the hand. As the mass of the Elephant increases, the 'tick' becomes smaller, requiring more hits to traverse the Pi-arc of the circle.

section_6.title: Conclusion: The Final Tally
section_6.content: Summarize how the number of collisions is the integer part of (Pi / angle). As the mass ratio becomes a power of 100, the angle becomes perfectly aligned with the decimal positions of Pi.
section_6.example: A final high-speed montage: M = 1,000,000m. The counter blurs as the blocks vibrate, finally stopping at exactly 3,141. The screen overlays the digits of Pi over the block counter.

section_1.title: The Setup: A Curious Experiment
lecture_lines: Imagine two blocks sliding on a frictionless floor.
A wall sits on the far left side.
A large block collides with a stationary small block.
We count every collision between blocks and the wall.
Watch as the collision count reveals digits of Pi.
animations: Create a white wall (#FFFFFF) on the left and a floor line. Draw a small block (#00FF00) labeled 'm' and a large block (#0000FF) labeled 'M'.
The large block (#0000FF) slides from the right edge toward the stationary small block (#00FF00).
A counter (#FFFF00) appears at the top. Flash the counter with numbers 3, 31, 314 as the blocks collide.

section_2.title: Prerequisite Knowledge: The Laws of the Game
lecture_lines: Energy conservation keeps the system's total speed restricted.
Momentum conservation governs how velocity transfers between blocks.
These physical laws define the rules of every hit.
animations: Display 'Energy Conservation' in green (#00FF00) and 'Momentum Conservation' in blue (#0000FF) at the top of the screen.
Show a pulsing battery icon (#00FF00) in the center, representing the system's total kinetic energy.
Draw directional arrows (#0000FF) between the blocks during a collision to show momentum transfer.

section_3.title: Mapping to Phase Space: The Velocity Vector
lecture_lines: We plot velocities on a two-dimensional graph.
Each point represents the current state of both blocks.
Collisions cause this state point to jump around.
animations: Create a 2D coordinate system. Label the X-axis 'v1' in blue (#0000FF) and the Y-axis 'v2' in green (#00FF00).
Plot a bright yellow point (#FFFF00) at the initial velocity coordinates (v1_initial, 0).
When the small block hits the wall, the point (#FFFF00) instantly reflects across the X-axis.
When the blocks collide, the point (#FFFF00) moves along a diagonal line to its new velocity state.
A thin white line (#FFFFFF) trails behind the point, showing the path of the system's state.

section_4.title: The Geometry of Energy: Stretching the Circle
lecture_lines: Energy conservation forms an elliptical path on our graph.
We rescale the axes to simplify the geometry.
The ellipse transforms into a perfect, uniform circle.
The system's state now moves along this circular boundary.
Geometry reveals hidden patterns in the block dynamics.
animations: Draw a horizontal green ellipse (#00FF00) centered at the origin, representing the initial energy equation.
Display the scaling factors sqrt(M) and sqrt(m) next to the v1 and v2 axes.
Animate the green ellipse stretching vertically until it becomes a perfect cyan circle (#00FFFF).
Highlight the perimeter of the cyan circle (#00FFFF) with a bright glow to show the state constraint.
Fade in the symbol 'Pi' (#FFFF00) at the center of the circle.

section_5.title: The Secret Angle: Why Pi?
lecture_lines: Each collision rotates the state by a constant angle.
This angle depends on the ratio of block masses.
We count how many jumps fit within the circle.
Total collisions equal the total arc divided by angle.
Half the circle represents Pi radians of total rotation.
animations: Show the yellow state point (#FFFF00) performing discrete jumps along the arc of the cyan circle (#00FFFF).
Draw two radial lines from the center to consecutive points, highlighting the angle 'theta' in magenta (#FF00FF).
Show the angle 'theta' (#FF00FF) getting smaller as the mass M is increased visually.
Highlight the top half of the circle's arc in white (#FFFFFF) to represent the 180-degree (Pi) path.
Display the calculation 'Hits = Pi / Theta' in white (#FFFFFF) as the point completes its traversal.

section_6.title: Conclusion: The Final Tally
lecture_lines: Larger mass ratios create smaller, more precise angles.
The collision count perfectly matches the digits of Pi.
A surprising link between simple physics and mathematical constants.
animations: Display the block simulation again with a collision counter showing '3141' in yellow (#FFFF00).
Show a table mapping mass ratios (1, 100, 10000) to collision counts (3, 31, 314) in white (#FFFFFF).
Fade out everything except the collision counter, which transforms into the first digits of Pi (#FFFF00).

from manim import *
import numpy as np

class TeachingScene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text(f"- {line}", font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (6x6 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                x = 0.5 + j * 1
                y = 2.2 - i * 1
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

    def place_in_area(self, mobject, top_left, bottom_right, scale_factor=1.0):
        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
        
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject

class Section5Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        self.setup_layout("The Secret Angle: Why Pi?", [
            "Each collision rotates the state by a constant angle.",
            "This angle depends on the ratio of block masses.",
            "We count how many jumps fit within the circle.",
            "Total collisions equal the total arc divided by angle.",
            "Half the circle represents Pi radians of total rotation."
        ])

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.lecture[0].set_color(YELLOW)
        
        # Circle setup
        circle = Circle(radius=2, color="#00FFFF") # Cyan
        self.place_in_area(circle, "A1", "F6", scale_factor=0.8)
        center = circle.get_center()
        self.add(circle)

        # State point
        state_point = Dot(color="#FFFF00") # Yellow
        state_point.move_to(circle.point_at_angle(0))
        self.add(state_point)

        # Constant angle jumps
        theta_val = 30 * DEGREES
        num_jumps = 4
        
        for i in range(1, num_jumps + 1):
            target_angle = i * theta_val
            self.play(
                state_point.animate.move_to(circle.point_at_angle(target_angle)),
                run_time=0.5
            )
        
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.lecture[0].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[1].set_color("#FF00FF") # Magenta

        # Show angle theta
        p1 = circle.point_at_angle(0)
        p2 = circle.point_at_angle(theta_val)
        
        radial_line1 = Line(center, p1, color=WHITE, stroke_width=2)
        radial_line2 = Line(center, p2, color=WHITE, stroke_width=2)
        
        angle_arc = Arc(radius=0.5, start_angle=0, angle=theta_val, arc_center=center, color="#FF00FF")
        theta_label = MathTex(r"\theta", color="#FF00FF", font_size=24)
        # Position label near arc
        theta_label.move_to(center + 0.8 * np.array([np.cos(theta_val/2), np.sin(theta_val/2), 0]))

        self.play(Create(radial_line1), Create(radial_line2), Create(angle_arc), Write(theta_label))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.lecture[1].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[2].set_color(YELLOW)

        # Show mass M increasing -> theta decreasing
        # We'll just animate theta_val shrinking
        new_theta = 15 * DEGREES
        
        # Update components
        new_p2 = circle.point_at_angle(new_theta)
        new_radial_line2 = Line(center, new_p2, color=WHITE, stroke_width=2)
        new_angle_arc = Arc(radius=0.5, start_angle=0, angle=new_theta, arc_center=center, color="#FF00FF")
        new_theta_label_pos = center + 0.8 * np.array([np.cos(new_theta/2), np.sin(new_theta/2), 0])

        self.play(
            Transform(radial_line2, new_radial_line2),
            Transform(angle_arc, new_angle_arc),
            theta_label.animate.move_to(new_theta_label_pos),
            state_point.animate.move_to(circle.point_at_angle(new_theta)),
            run_time=1.5
        )
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 4 ===
        self.lecture[2].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[3].set_color(WHITE) # Using White as requested in prompt "in white (#FFFFFF)"

        # Calculation display
        calc = MathTex(r"\text{Hits} = \frac{\pi}{\theta}", color=WHITE, font_size=32)
        self.place_at_grid(calc, "F3", scale_factor=1.0)
        
        self.play(Write(calc))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 5 ===
        self.lecture[3].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[4].set_color("#FFFFFF") # White

        # Highlight top half arc
        pi_arc = Arc(radius=2, start_angle=0, angle=PI, arc_center=center, color=WHITE, stroke_width=6)
        
        # We need a label for Pi radians
        pi_label = MathTex(r"\pi \text{ radians}", color=WHITE, font_size=28)
        self.place_at_grid(pi_label, "B3", scale_factor=1.0)

        self.play(Create(pi_arc), Write(pi_label))
        
        # Final point traversal to show it fits within Pi
        # Let's do a few more jumps along the Pi arc
        for i in range(2, 13): # 12 * 15 degrees = 180 degrees
            self.play(
                state_point.animate.move_to(circle.point_at_angle(i * new_theta)),
                run_time=0.2
            )

        self.wait(2)

        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2

        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject

            "These physical laws define the rules of every hit."
        ]
        
        self.setup_layout(title, lines)

        # Colors
        GREEN = "#00FF00"
        BLUE = "#0000FF"

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        # Display 'Energy Conservation' in green (#00FF00) and 'Momentum Conservation' in blue (#0000FF) at the top
        energy_label = Text("Energy Conservation", color=GREEN, font_size=24)
        momentum_label = Text("Momentum Conservation", color=BLUE, font_size=24)
        
        self.place_in_area(energy_label, "A1", "A3", scale_factor=0.8)
        self.place_in_area(momentum_label, "A4", "A6", scale_factor=0.8)

        self.lecture[0].set_color(GREEN)
        self.play(FadeIn(energy_label), FadeIn(momentum_label))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        # Show a pulsing battery icon (#00FF00) in the center
        # Creating a battery icon
        battery_body = Rectangle(width=1.5, height=0.8, color=GREEN, stroke_width=4)
        battery_tip = Rectangle(width=0.2, height=0.4, color=GREEN, fill_opacity=1).next_to(battery_body, RIGHT, buff=0)
        battery_fill = Rectangle(width=1.2, height=0.6, fill_color=GREEN, fill_opacity=0.8, stroke_width=0).move_to(battery_body)
        battery = VGroup(battery_body, battery_tip, battery_fill)
        
        self.place_in_area(battery, "B3", "D4", scale_factor=1.0)
        
        # Pulse mechanism using ValueTracker
        pulse_tracker = ValueTracker(0)
        def pulse_updater(m):
            # Scale factor oscillating between 0.95 and 1.05
            val = pulse_tracker.get_value()
            scale = 1 + 0.05 * np.sin(val * PI * 2)
            m.scale(scale / m.pulse_prev_scale)
            m.pulse_prev_scale = scale

        self.lecture[2].set_color(BLUE)
        self.play(FadeIn(block_large), FadeIn(block_small))

    def construct(self):
        lecture_lines = [
            "Imagine two blocks sliding on a frictionless floor.",
            "A wall sits on the far left side.",
            "A large block collides with a stationary small block.",
            "We count every collision between blocks and the wall.",
            "Watch as the collision count reveals digits of Pi."
        ]
        self.setup_layout("The Setup: A Curious Experiment", lecture_lines)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[0].animate.set_color(YELLOW))
        
        # Floor
        floor = Line(self.grid["E1"] + LEFT*0.5, self.grid["E6"] + RIGHT*0.5, color=WHITE)
        
        # Small block 'm'
        small_block = Square(side_length=0.4, color="#00FF00", fill_opacity=0.5)
        self.place_at_grid(small_block, "E2")
        small_label = MathTex("m", color="#00FF00").scale(0.8)
        small_label.next_to(small_block, UP, buff=0.1)
        
        # Large block 'M'
        large_block = Square(side_length=0.8, color="#0000FF", fill_opacity=0.5)
        self.place_at_grid(large_block, "E5")
        large_label = MathTex("M", color="#0000FF").scale(0.8)
        large_label.next_to(large_block, UP, buff=0.1)

        self.play(Create(floor), Create(small_block), Write(small_label), Create(large_block), Write(large_label))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.play(
            self.lecture[0].animate.set_color(WHITE),
            self.lecture[1].animate.set_color(YELLOW)
        )

        self.wait(1)

        self.play(
            self.lecture[1].animate.set_color(WHITE),
            self.lecture[2].animate.set_color(YELLOW)
        )
        
        # Move large block toward small block
        target_pos = self.grid["E3"]
        self.play(
            large_block.animate.move_to(target_pos),
            large_label.animate.next_to(target_pos, UP, buff=0.1),
            run_time=2,
            rate_func=linear
        )
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 4 ===

            self.lecture[2].animate.set_color(WHITE),
            self.lecture[3].animate.set_color(YELLOW)

        )

                counter_val.animate.set_value(val),
                Flash(counter_val, color="#FFFF00", flash_radius=0.3),
                run_time=1
            )
            self.wait(0.5)

        self.play(self.lecture[4].animate.set_color(WHITE))
        self.wait(2)

    def construct(self):
        self.setup_layout("The Secret Angle: Why Pi?", [
            "Each collision rotates the state by a constant angle.",
            "This angle depends on the ratio of block masses.",
            "We count how many jumps fit within the circle.",
            "Total collisions equal the total arc divided by angle.",
            "Half the circle represents Pi radians of total rotation."
        ])

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.lecture[0].set_color(YELLOW)
        
        # Circle setup
        circle = Circle(radius=2, color="#00FFFF") # Cyan
        self.place_in_area(circle, "A1", "F6", scale_factor=0.8)

        # State point

        state_point.move_to(circle.point_at_angle(0))
        self.add(state_point)

        # Constant angle jumps
        theta_val = 30 * DEGREES
        num_jumps = 4
        
        for i in range(1, num_jumps + 1):
            target_angle = i * theta_val
            self.play(
                state_point.animate.move_to(circle.point_at_angle(target_angle)),
                run_time=0.5
            )
        
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.lecture[0].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[1].set_color("#FF00FF") # Magenta

        # Show angle theta
        p1 = circle.point_at_angle(0)
        p2 = circle.point_at_angle(theta_val)
        
        radial_line1 = Line(center, p1, color=WHITE, stroke_width=2)
        radial_line2 = Line(center, p2, color=WHITE, stroke_width=2)
        
        angle_arc = Arc(radius=0.5, start_angle=0, angle=theta_val, arc_center=center, color="#FF00FF")
        theta_label = MathTex(r"\theta", color="#FF00FF", font_size=24)

        self.wait(1)

        self.lecture[1].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[2].set_color(YELLOW)

        # Show mass M increasing -> theta decreasing
        # We'll just animate theta_val shrinking
        new_theta = 15 * DEGREES
        
        # Update components
        new_p2 = circle.point_at_angle(new_theta)
        new_radial_line2 = Line(center, new_p2, color=WHITE, stroke_width=2)
        new_angle_arc = Arc(radius=0.5, start_angle=0, angle=new_theta, arc_center=center, color="#FF00FF")

        self.play(
            Transform(radial_line2, new_radial_line2),
            Transform(angle_arc, new_angle_arc),
            theta_label.animate.move_to(new_theta_label_pos),
            state_point.animate.move_to(circle.point_at_angle(new_theta)),
            run_time=1.5
        )
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 4 ===
        self.lecture[2].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[3].set_color(WHITE) # Using White as requested in prompt "in white (#FFFFFF)"

        calc = MathTex(r"\text{Hits} = \frac{\pi}{\theta}", color=WHITE, font_size=32)
        self.place_at_grid(calc, "F3", scale_factor=1.0)
        
        self.play(Write(calc))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 5 ===
        self.lecture[3].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[4].set_color("#FFFFFF") # White

        # Highlight top half arc
        pi_arc = Arc(radius=2, start_angle=0, angle=PI, arc_center=center, color=WHITE, stroke_width=6)
        
        # We need a label for Pi radians
        pi_label = MathTex(r"\pi \text{ radians}", color=WHITE, font_size=28)
        self.place_at_grid(pi_label, "B3", scale_factor=1.0)

        self.play(Create(pi_arc), Write(pi_label))
        
        # Final point traversal to show it fits within Pi
        # Let's do a few more jumps along the Pi arc
        for i in range(2, 13): # 12 * 15 degrees = 180 degrees

I have completed the Manim code for **Section 5: The Secret Angle: Why Pi?**.

### Key Implementation Details:
- **Visual Anchor System**: The circle and animations are positioned using the 6x6 grid system. The circle is centered within the main animation area, and labels are placed at specific grid points (e.g., `F3` for the formula, `B3` for the $\pi$ label).
- **State Point Jumps**: A yellow state point (#FFFF00) performs discrete jumps along a cyan circle (#00FFFF), representing collisions.
- **Angle Visualization**: A magenta angle $\theta$ (#FF00FF) is shown between radial lines. The code demonstrates $\theta$ decreasing as the mass ratio changes.
- **Pi Arc Traversal**: The top half of the circle is highlighted in white (#FFFFFF) to represent the total rotation of $\pi$ radians, and the state point traverses this arc to illustrate the counting of hits.
- **Formula**: The relationship $\text{Hits} = \frac{\pi}{\theta}$ is displayed at the end of the section.
- **Lecture Alignment**: Each lecture line is highlighted with a color matching its corresponding animation elements (Yellow for movement, Magenta for the angle, and White for the mathematical constants and summary).

The code is optimized for performance by using standard Manim mobjects and animations within the 180-second render limit.

```python
from manim import *
import numpy as np

class TeachingScene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text(f"- {line}", font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (6x6 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                x = 0.5 + j * 1
                y = 2.2 - i * 1
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

    def place_in_area(self, mobject, top_left, bottom_right, scale_factor=1.0):
        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
        
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject

class Section5Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        self.setup_layout("The Secret Angle: Why Pi?", [
            "Each collision rotates the state by a constant angle.",
            "This angle depends on the ratio of block masses.",
            "We count how many jumps fit within the circle.",
            "Total collisions equal the total arc divided by angle.",
            "Half the circle represents Pi radians of total rotation."
        ])

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.lecture[0].set_color(YELLOW)
        
        # Circle setup
        circle = Circle(radius=2, color="#00FFFF") # Cyan
        self.place_in_area(circle, "A1", "F6", scale_factor=0.8)
        center = circle.get_center()
        self.add(circle)

        # State point
        state_point = Dot(color="#FFFF00") # Yellow
        state_point.move_to(circle.point_at_angle(0))
        self.add(state_point)

        # Constant angle jumps
        theta_val = 30 * DEGREES
        num_jumps = 4
        
        for i in range(1, num_jumps + 1):
            target_angle = i * theta_val
            self.play(
                state_point.animate.move_to(circle.point_at_angle(target_angle)),
                run_time=0.5
            )
        
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.lecture[0].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[1].set_color("#FF00FF") # Magenta

        # Show angle theta
        p1 = circle.point_at_angle(0)
        p2 = circle.point_at_angle(theta_val)
        
        radial_line1 = Line(center, p1, color=WHITE, stroke_width=2)
        radial_line2 = Line(center, p2, color=WHITE, stroke_width=2)
        
        angle_arc = Arc(radius=0.5, start_angle=0, angle=theta_val, arc_center=center, color="#FF00FF")
        theta_label = MathTex(r"\theta", color="#FF00FF", font_size=24)
        # Position label near arc
        theta_label.move_to(center + 0.8 * np.array([np.cos(theta_val/2), np.sin(theta_val/2), 0]))

        self.play(Create(radial_line1), Create(radial_line2), Create(angle_arc), Write(theta_label))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.lecture[1].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[2].set_color(YELLOW)

        # Show mass M increasing -> theta decreasing
        new_theta = 15 * DEGREES
        
        # Update components
        new_p2 = circle.point_at_angle(new_theta)
        new_radial_line2 = Line(center, new_p2, color=WHITE, stroke_width=2)
        new_angle_arc = Arc(radius=0.5, start_angle=0, angle=new_theta, arc_center=center, color="#FF00FF")
        new_theta_label_pos = center + 0.8 * np.array([np.cos(new_theta/2), np.sin(new_theta/2), 0])

        self.play(
            Transform(radial_line2, new_radial_line2),
            Transform(angle_arc, new_angle_arc),
            theta_label.animate.move_to(new_theta_label_pos),
            state_point.animate.move_to(circle.point_at_angle(new_theta)),
            run_time=1.5
        )
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 4 ===
        self.lecture[2].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[3].set_color(WHITE) 

        # Calculation display
        calc = MathTex(r"\text{Hits} = \frac{\pi}{\theta}", color=WHITE, font_size=32)
        self.place_at_grid(calc, "F3", scale_factor=1.0)
        
        self.play(Write(calc))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 5 ===
        self.lecture[3].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[4].set_color("#FFFFFF") # White

        # Highlight top half arc
        pi_arc = Arc(radius=2, start_angle=0, angle=PI, arc_center=center, color=WHITE, stroke_width=6)
        
        # Label for Pi radians
        pi_label = MathTex(r"\pi \text{ radians}", color=WHITE, font_size=28)
        self.place_at_grid(pi_label, "B3", scale_factor=1.0)

        self.play(Create(pi_arc), Write(pi_label))
        
        # Final point traversal to show it fits within Pi
        for i in range(2, 13): # 12 * 15 degrees = 180 degrees
            self.play(
                state_point.animate.move_to(circle.point_at_angle(i * new_theta)),
                run_time=0.2
            )

        self.wait(2)

class Section1Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        lecture_lines = [
            "Imagine two blocks sliding on a frictionless floor.",
            "A wall sits on the far left side.",
            "A large block collides with a stationary small block.",
            "We count every collision between blocks and the wall.",
            "Watch as the collision count reveals digits of Pi."
        ]
        self.setup_layout("The Setup: A Curious Experiment", lecture_lines)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[0].animate.set_color(YELLOW))
        
        # Floor
        floor = Line(self.grid["E1"] + LEFT*0.5, self.grid["E6"] + RIGHT*0.5, color=WHITE)
        
        # Small block 'm'
        small_block = Square(side_length=0.4, color="#00FF00", fill_opacity=0.5)
        self.place_at_grid(small_block, "E2")
        small_label = MathTex("m", color="#00FF00").scale(0.8)
        small_label.next_to(small_block, UP, buff=0.1)
        
        # Large block 'M'
        large_block = Square(side_length=0.8, color="#0000FF", fill_opacity=0.5)
        self.place_at_grid(large_block, "E5")
        large_label = MathTex("M", color="#0000FF").scale(0.8)
        large_label.next_to(large_block, UP, buff=0.1)

        self.play(Create(floor), Create(small_block), Write(small_label), Create(large_block), Write(large_label))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.play(
            self.lecture[0].animate.set_color(WHITE),
            self.lecture[1].animate.set_color(YELLOW)
        )
        
        # Wall
        wall = Line(self.grid["C1"] + LEFT*0.5, self.grid["E1"] + LEFT*0.5 + DOWN*0.2, color="#FFFFFF", stroke_width=6)
        self.play(Create(wall))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.play(
            self.lecture[1].animate.set_color(WHITE),
            self.lecture[2].animate.set_color(YELLOW)
        )
        
        # Move large block toward small block
        target_pos = self.grid["E3"]
        self.play(
            large_block.animate.move_to(target_pos),
            large_label.animate.next_to(target_pos, UP, buff=0.1),
            run_time=2,
            rate_func=linear
        )
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 4 ===
        self.play(
            self.lecture[2].animate.set_color(WHITE),
            self.lecture[3].animate.set_color(YELLOW)
        )
        
        # Counter appears
        counter_label = Text("Collisions:", font_size=24, color="#FFFF00")
        self.place_at_grid(counter_label, "A3")
        counter_val = Integer(0, color="#FFFF00")
        counter_val.next_to(counter_label, RIGHT, buff=0.2)
        
        self.play(Write(counter_label), Write(counter_val))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 5 ===
        self.play(
            self.lecture[3].animate.set_color(WHITE),
            self.lecture[4].animate.set_color(YELLOW)
        )
        
        # Flash numbers 3, 31, 314
        for val in [3, 31, 314]:
            self.play(
                counter_val.animate.set_value(val),
                Flash(counter_val, color="#FFFF00", flash_radius=0.3),
                run_time=1
            )
            self.wait(0.5)

        self.play(self.lecture[4].animate.set_color(WHITE))
        self.wait(2)

        mobject.scale(scale_factor)

class Section3Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        self.setup_layout("Mapping to Phase Space: The Velocity Vector", [
            "We plot velocities on a two-dimensional graph.",
            "Each point represents the current state of both blocks.",
            "Collisions cause this state point to jump around."
        ])
        
        # Colors
        V1_COLOR = "#0000FF"
        V2_COLOR = "#00FF00"
        POINT_COLOR = "#FFFF00"
        TRAIL_COLOR = "#FFFFFF"
        HIGHLIGHT_COLOR = YELLOW

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.lecture[0].set_color(HIGHLIGHT_COLOR)
        
        # Create axes with colors specified in storyboard
        axes = Axes(
            x_range=[-2.2, 2.2, 1],
            y_range=[-2.2, 2.2, 1],
            x_length=4,
            y_length=4,
            axis_config={"include_tip": True},
            x_axis_config={"color": V1_COLOR},
            y_axis_config={"color": V2_COLOR}
        )
        x_label = MathTex("v_1", color=V1_COLOR).scale(0.8)
        y_label = MathTex("v_2", color=V2_COLOR).scale(0.8)
        
        # Positioning axes in area B2 to E5 (central part of the right side)
        self.place_in_area(axes, "B2", "E5")
        
        # Position labels near axes tips within 1 unit
        x_label.next_to(axes.x_axis.get_end(), DOWN, buff=0.1)
        y_label.next_to(axes.y_axis.get_end(), LEFT, buff=0.1)
        
        axes_group = VGroup(axes, x_label, y_label)
        self.play(Create(axes_group))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.lecture[0].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[1].set_color(HIGHLIGHT_COLOR)
        
        # Initial point at (v1_initial, 0). 
        v1_initial = -1.2
        v2_initial = 0
        point = Dot(axes.c2p(v1_initial, v2_initial), color=POINT_COLOR, radius=0.08)
        
        # The trail follows the point and uses #FFFFFF
        trail = TracedPath(point.get_center, stroke_color=TRAIL_COLOR, stroke_width=2)
        
        # State label that follows the point
        point_label = MathTex("(v_1, v_2)", color=POINT_COLOR).scale(0.7)
        point_label.next_to(point, UP, buff=0.1)
        
        # Keep label centered over the moving point
        point_label.add_updater(lambda d: d.next_to(point, UP, buff=0.1))

        self.add(trail)
        self.play(FadeIn(point), Write(point_label))
        self.wait(2)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.lecture[1].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[2].set_color(HIGHLIGHT_COLOR)
        
        # Physics logic for animation visualization (m1=5, m2=1)
        m1, m2 = 5.0, 1.0
        
        def get_next_velocities(v1, v2, type="block"):
            if type == "block":
                # Elastic collision: momentum and energy conservation
                v1_new = ((m1 - m2) / (m1 + m2)) * v1 + (2 * m2 / (m1 + m2)) * v2
                v2_new = (2 * m1 / (m1 + m2)) * v1 - ((m1 - m2) / (m1 + m2)) * v2
                return v1_new, v2_new
            else:
                # Wall hit: v2 flips sign (reflection across X-axis)
                return v1, -v2

        # Step 1: Blocks collide (moves along diagonal)
        v1_1, v2_1 = get_next_velocities(v1_initial, v2_initial, "block")
        self.play(point.animate.move_to(axes.c2p(v1_1, v2_1)), run_time=1.2, rate_func=linear)
        self.wait(0.3)
        
        # Step 2: Small block hits wall (instantly reflects across X-axis)
        v1_2, v2_2 = get_next_velocities(v1_1, v2_1, "wall")
        self.play(point.animate.move_to(axes.c2p(v1_2, v2_2)), run_time=0.6, rate_func=linear)
        self.wait(0.3)
        
        # Step 3: Blocks collide again
        v1_3, v2_3 = get_next_velocities(v1_2, v2_2, "block")
        self.play(point.animate.move_to(axes.c2p(v1_3, v2_3)), run_time=1.2, rate_func=linear)
        self.wait(0.3)

        # Step 4: Wall hit
        v1_4, v2_4 = get_next_velocities(v1_3, v2_3, "wall")
        self.play(point.animate.move_to(axes.c2p(v1_4, v2_4)), run_time=0.6, rate_func=linear)
        self.wait(1)
        
        # Clean up
        point_label.clear_updaters()
        self.play(FadeOut(point_label), self.lecture[2].animate.set_color(WHITE))
        self.wait(2)

class Section3Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        self.setup_layout("Mapping to Phase Space: The Velocity Vector", [
            "We plot velocities on a two-dimensional graph.",
            "Each point represents the current state of both blocks.",
            "Collisions cause this state point to jump around."
        ])
        
        # Colors
        V1_COLOR = "#0000FF"
        V2_COLOR = "#00FF00"
        POINT_COLOR = "#FFFF00"
        TRAIL_COLOR = "#FFFFFF"
        HIGHLIGHT_COLOR = YELLOW

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.lecture[0].set_color(HIGHLIGHT_COLOR)
        
        # Create axes with colors specified in storyboard
        axes = Axes(
            x_range=[-2.2, 2.2, 1],
            y_range=[-2.2, 2.2, 1],
            x_length=4,
            y_length=4,
            axis_config={"include_tip": True},
            x_axis_config={"color": V1_COLOR},
            y_axis_config={"color": V2_COLOR}
        )
        x_label = MathTex("v_1", color=V1_COLOR).scale(0.8)
        y_label = MathTex("v_2", color=V2_COLOR).scale(0.8)
        
        # Positioning axes in area B2 to E5 (central part of the right side)
        self.place_in_area(axes, "B2", "E5")
        
        # Position labels near axes tips within 1 unit
        x_label.next_to(axes.x_axis.get_end(), DOWN, buff=0.1)
        y_label.next_to(axes.y_axis.get_end(), LEFT, buff=0.1)
        
        axes_group = VGroup(axes, x_label, y_label)
        self.play(Create(axes_group))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.lecture[0].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[1].set_color(HIGHLIGHT_COLOR)
        
        # Initial point at (v1_initial, 0). 
        v1_initial = -1.2
        v2_initial = 0
        point = Dot(axes.c2p(v1_initial, v2_initial), color=POINT_COLOR, radius=0.08)
        
        # The trail follows the point and uses #FFFFFF
        trail = TracedPath(point.get_center, stroke_color=TRAIL_COLOR, stroke_width=2)
        
        # State label that follows the point
        point_label = MathTex("(v_1, v_2)", color=POINT_COLOR).scale(0.7)
        point_label.next_to(point, UP, buff=0.1)
        
        # Keep label centered over the moving point
        point_label.add_updater(lambda d: d.next_to(point, UP, buff=0.1))

        self.add(trail)
        self.play(FadeIn(point), Write(point_label))
        self.wait(2)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.lecture[1].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[2].set_color(HIGHLIGHT_COLOR)
        
        # Physics logic for animation visualization (m1=5, m2=1)
        m1, m2 = 5.0, 1.0
        
        def get_next_velocities(v1, v2, type="block"):
            if type == "block":
                # Elastic collision: momentum and energy conservation
                v1_new = ((m1 - m2) / (m1 + m2)) * v1 + (2 * m2 / (m1 + m2)) * v2
                v2_new = (2 * m1 / (m1 + m2)) * v1 - ((m1 - m2) / (m1 + m2)) * v2
                return v1_new, v2_new
            else:
                # Wall hit: v2 flips sign (reflection across X-axis)
                return v1, -v2

        # Step 1: Blocks collide (moves along diagonal)
        v1_1, v2_1 = get_next_velocities(v1_initial, v2_initial, "block")
        self.play(point.animate.move_to(axes.c2p(v1_1, v2_1)), run_time=1.2, rate_func=linear)
        self.wait(0.3)
        
        # Step 2: Small block hits wall (instantly reflects across X-axis)
        v1_2, v2_2 = get_next_velocities(v1_1, v2_1, "wall")
        self.play(point.animate.move_to(axes.c2p(v1_2, v2_2)), run_time=0.6, rate_func=linear)
        self.wait(0.3)
        
        # Step 3: Blocks collide again
        v1_3, v2_3 = get_next_velocities(v1_2, v2_2, "block")
        self.play(point.animate.move_to(axes.c2p(v1_3, v2_3)), run_time=1.2, rate_func=linear)
        self.wait(0.3)

        # Step 4: Wall hit
        v1_4, v2_4 = get_next_velocities(v1_3, v2_3, "wall")
        self.play(point.animate.move_to(axes.c2p(v1_4, v2_4)), run_time=0.6, rate_func=linear)
        self.wait(1)
        
        # Clean up
        point_label.clear_updaters()
        self.play(FadeOut(point_label), self.lecture[2].animate.set_color(WHITE))
        self.wait(2)

import numpy as np

        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text(line, font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (6x6 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                x = 0.5 + j * 1
                y = 2.2 - i * 1
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]

        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2

section_1.title: The Setup: A Curious Experiment
section_1.content: Introduce the physical scenario: A frictionless surface, a wall on the left, and two blocks. A small block sits still, and a much larger block comes charging in from the right. We count every single collision (Block vs. Block and Block vs. Wall).
section_1.example: Imagine a giant Elephant-shaped block (Mass M) sliding toward a tiny Ant-shaped block (Mass m). If M = m, there are 3 collisions. If M = 100m, there are 31. If M = 10,000m, there are 314. The digits of Pi appear magically.

section_2.title: Prerequisite Knowledge: The Laws of the Game
section_2.content: Explain the two fundamental physics principles governing these collisions: Conservation of Energy (the system doesn't lose 'juice') and Conservation of Momentum (the 'push' is transferred). Visualize these as two mathematical equations that must always be satisfied.
section_2.example: Use an animation of a pulsing battery icon for 'Energy' and a directional arrow for 'Momentum' to show how they transfer between the Elephant and the Ant during a hit.

section_3.title: Mapping to Phase Space: The Velocity Vector
section_3.content: Instead of watching the blocks move in space, we plot their velocities on a graph. Let the x-axis be the velocity of the big block (v1) and the y-axis be the velocity of the small block (v2). Every state of the system is just a single point on this graph.
section_3.example: Show a 2D coordinate system where the 'state' point moves every time a collision occurs. A wall hit flips the y-coordinate; a block hit moves the point along a specific path.

section_4.title: The Geometry of Energy: Stretching the Circle
section_4.content: Explain that because Conservation of Energy (1/2 Mv1² + 1/2 mv2² = Constant) looks like the equation of an ellipse, we can 'rescale' the axes by the square root of the masses to turn that ellipse into a perfect circle.
section_4.example: An animation showing a squashed oval (ellipse) being physically stretched vertically until it becomes a perfect, glowing circle. The 'state' of our blocks is now a point trapped on the rim of this circle.

section_5.title: The Secret Angle: Why Pi?
section_5.content: Each collision corresponds to a 'jump' along the arc of this circle. Because of the mass ratio, each jump covers a tiny, constant angle. We count how many jumps it takes to go halfway around the circle (180 degrees or Pi radians) before the blocks move away from each other forever.
section_5.example: Visualize the circle as a clock face. Each collision is a 'tick' of the hand. As the mass of the Elephant increases, the 'tick' becomes smaller, requiring more hits to traverse the Pi-arc of the circle.

section_6.title: Conclusion: The Final Tally
section_6.content: Summarize how the number of collisions is the integer part of (Pi / angle). As the mass ratio becomes a power of 100, the angle becomes perfectly aligned with the decimal positions of Pi.
section_6.example: A final high-speed montage: M = 1,000,000m. The counter blurs as the blocks vibrate, finally stopping at exactly 3,141. The screen overlays the digits of Pi over the block counter.

import numpy as np

class TeachingScene(Scene):

        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)

            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                x = 0.5 + j * 1
                y = 2.2 - i * 1
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
        
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject

class Section2Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        # Data from storyboard
        title = "Prerequisite Knowledge: The Laws of the Game"
        lines = [
            "Energy conservation keeps the system's total speed restricted.",
            "Momentum conservation governs how velocity transfers between blocks.",
            "These physical laws define the rules of every hit."
        ]
        
        self.setup_layout(title, lines)

        # Colors
        GREEN = "#00FF00"
        BLUE = "#0000FF"

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        # Display 'Energy Conservation' in green (#00FF00) and 'Momentum Conservation' in blue (#0000FF) at the top
        energy_label = Text("Energy Conservation", color=GREEN, font_size=24)
        momentum_label = Text("Momentum Conservation", color=BLUE, font_size=24)
        
        self.place_in_area(energy_label, "A1", "A3", scale_factor=0.8)
        self.place_in_area(momentum_label, "A4", "A6", scale_factor=0.8)

        self.lecture[0].set_color(GREEN)
        self.play(FadeIn(energy_label), FadeIn(momentum_label))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        # Show a pulsing battery icon (#00FF00) in the center
        # Creating a battery icon
        battery_body = Rectangle(width=1.5, height=0.8, color=GREEN, stroke_width=4)
        battery_tip = Rectangle(width=0.2, height=0.4, color=GREEN, fill_opacity=1).next_to(battery_body, RIGHT, buff=0)
        battery_fill = Rectangle(width=1.2, height=0.6, fill_color=GREEN, fill_opacity=0.8, stroke_width=0).move_to(battery_body)
        battery = VGroup(battery_body, battery_tip, battery_fill)
        
        self.place_in_area(battery, "B3", "D4", scale_factor=1.0)
        
        # Pulse mechanism using ValueTracker
        pulse_tracker = ValueTracker(0)
        def pulse_updater(m):
            # Scale factor oscillating between 0.95 and 1.05
            val = pulse_tracker.get_value()
            scale = 1 + 0.05 * np.sin(val * PI * 2)
            m.scale(scale / m.pulse_prev_scale)
            m.pulse_prev_scale = scale
            
        battery.pulse_prev_scale = 1.0
        battery.add_updater(pulse_updater)
        
        self.lecture[1].set_color(GREEN)
        self.play(FadeIn(battery))
        self.play(pulse_tracker.animate.set_value(2), run_time=2, rate_func=linear)
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        # Draw directional arrows (#0000FF) between the blocks during a collision
        # Represent blocks
        block_large = Square(side_length=1.0, color=WHITE, fill_opacity=0.3)
        block_small = Square(side_length=0.5, color=WHITE, fill_opacity=0.3)
        
        self.place_at_grid(block_large, "E2", scale_factor=1.0)
        self.place_at_grid(block_small, "E5", scale_factor=1.0)
        
        # Momentum Arrow
        arrow = Arrow(start=self.grid["E2"], end=self.grid["E5"], color=BLUE, buff=0.2)
        
        self.lecture[2].set_color(BLUE)
        self.play(FadeIn(block_large), FadeIn(block_small))
        self.play(GrowArrow(arrow))
        
        # Simulate transfer: move arrow or flip it
        arrow_rev = Arrow(start=self.grid["E5"], end=self.grid["E2"], color=BLUE, buff=0.2)
        self.play(Transform(arrow, arrow_rev))
        self.wait(2)
        
        # Clean up updaters
        battery.remove_updater(pulse_updater)

class Section3Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        self.setup_layout("Mapping to Phase Space: The Velocity Vector", [
            "We plot velocities on a two-dimensional graph.",
            "Each point represents the current state of both blocks.",
            "Collisions cause this state point to jump around."
        ])
        
        # Colors
        V1_COLOR = "#0000FF"
        V2_COLOR = "#00FF00"
        POINT_COLOR = "#FFFF00"
        TRAIL_COLOR = "#FFFFFF"
        HIGHLIGHT_COLOR = YELLOW

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.lecture[0].set_color(HIGHLIGHT_COLOR)
        
        # Create axes with colors specified in storyboard
        axes = Axes(
            x_range=[-2.2, 2.2, 1],
            y_range=[-2.2, 2.2, 1],
            x_length=4,
            y_length=4,
            axis_config={"include_tip": True},
            x_axis_config={"color": V1_COLOR},
            y_axis_config={"color": V2_COLOR}
        )
        x_label = MathTex("v_1", color=V1_COLOR).scale(0.8)
        y_label = MathTex("v_2", color=V2_COLOR).scale(0.8)
        
        # Positioning axes in area B2 to E5 (central part of the right side)
        self.place_in_area(axes, "B2", "E5")
        
        # Position labels near axes tips within 1 unit
        x_label.next_to(axes.x_axis.get_end(), DOWN, buff=0.1)
        y_label.next_to(axes.y_axis.get_end(), LEFT, buff=0.1)
        
        axes_group = VGroup(axes, x_label, y_label)
        self.play(Create(axes_group))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.lecture[0].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[1].set_color(HIGHLIGHT_COLOR)
        
        # Initial point at (v1_initial, 0). 
        v1_initial = -1.2
        v2_initial = 0
        point = Dot(axes.c2p(v1_initial, v2_initial), color=POINT_COLOR, radius=0.08)
        
        # The trail follows the point and uses #FFFFFF
        trail = TracedPath(point.get_center, stroke_color=TRAIL_COLOR, stroke_width=2)
        
        # State label that follows the point
        point_label = MathTex("(v_1, v_2)", color=POINT_COLOR).scale(0.7)
        point_label.next_to(point, UP, buff=0.1)
        
        # Keep label centered over the moving point
        point_label.add_updater(lambda d: d.next_to(point, UP, buff=0.1))

        self.add(trail)
        self.play(FadeIn(point), Write(point_label))
        self.wait(2)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.lecture[1].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[2].set_color(HIGHLIGHT_COLOR)
        
        # Physics logic for animation visualization (m1=5, m2=1)
        m1, m2 = 5.0, 1.0
        
        def get_next_velocities(v1, v2, type="block"):
            if type == "block":
                # Elastic collision: momentum and energy conservation
                v1_new = ((m1 - m2) / (m1 + m2)) * v1 + (2 * m2 / (m1 + m2)) * v2
                v2_new = (2 * m1 / (m1 + m2)) * v1 - ((m1 - m2) / (m1 + m2)) * v2
                return v1_new, v2_new
            else:
                # Wall hit: v2 flips sign (reflection across X-axis)
                return v1, -v2

        # Step 1: Blocks collide (moves along diagonal)
        v1_1, v2_1 = get_next_velocities(v1_initial, v2_initial, "block")
        self.play(point.animate.move_to(axes.c2p(v1_1, v2_1)), run_time=1.2, rate_func=linear)
        self.wait(0.3)
        
        # Step 2: Small block hits wall (instantly reflects across X-axis)
        v1_2, v2_2 = get_next_velocities(v1_1, v2_1, "wall")
        self.play(point.animate.move_to(axes.c2p(v1_2, v2_2)), run_time=0.6, rate_func=linear)
        self.wait(0.3)
        
        # Step 3: Blocks collide again
        v1_3, v2_3 = get_next_velocities(v1_2, v2_2, "block")
        self.play(point.animate.move_to(axes.c2p(v1_3, v2_3)), run_time=1.2, rate_func=linear)
        self.wait(0.3)

        # Step 4: Wall hit
        v1_4, v2_4 = get_next_velocities(v1_3, v2_3, "wall")
        self.play(point.animate.move_to(axes.c2p(v1_4, v2_4)), run_time=0.6, rate_func=linear)
        self.wait(1)
        
        # Clean up
        point_label.clear_updaters()
        self.play(FadeOut(point_label), self.lecture[2].animate.set_color(WHITE))
        self.wait(2)

from manim import *
import numpy as np

class TeachingScene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text(line, font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (4x4 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                x = 0.5 + j * 1
                y = 2.2 - i * 1
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

    def place_in_area(self, mobject, top_left, bottom_right, scale_factor=1.0):
        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
        
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject

class Section5Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        self.setup_layout("The Secret Angle: Why Pi?", [
            "Each collision rotates the state by a constant angle.",
            "This angle depends on the ratio of block masses.",
            "We count how many jumps fit within the circle.",
            "Total collisions equal the total arc divided by angle.",
            "Half the circle represents Pi radians of total rotation."
        ])

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.lecture[0].set_color(YELLOW)
        
        # Circle setup
        circle = Circle(radius=2, color="#00FFFF") # Cyan
        self.place_in_area(circle, "A1", "F6", scale_factor=0.8)
        center = circle.get_center()
        self.add(circle)

        # State point
        state_point = Dot(color="#FFFF00") # Yellow
        state_point.move_to(circle.point_at_angle(0))
        self.add(state_point)

        # Constant angle jumps
        theta_val = 30 * DEGREES
        num_jumps = 4
        
        for i in range(1, num_jumps + 1):
            target_angle = i * theta_val
            self.play(
                state_point.animate.move_to(circle.point_at_angle(target_angle)),
                run_time=0.5
            )
        
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.lecture[0].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[1].set_color("#FF00FF") # Magenta

        # Show angle theta
        p1 = circle.point_at_angle(0)
        p2 = circle.point_at_angle(theta_val)
        
        radial_line1 = Line(center, p1, color=WHITE, stroke_width=2)
        radial_line2 = Line(center, p2, color=WHITE, stroke_width=2)
        
        angle_arc = Arc(radius=0.5, start_angle=0, angle=theta_val, arc_center=center, color="#FF00FF")
        theta_label = MathTex(r"\theta", color="#FF00FF", font_size=24)
        # Position label near arc
        theta_label.move_to(center + 0.8 * np.array([np.cos(theta_val/2), np.sin(theta_val/2), 0]))

        self.play(Create(radial_line1), Create(radial_line2), Create(angle_arc), Write(theta_label))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.lecture[1].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[2].set_color(YELLOW)

        # Show mass M increasing -> theta decreasing
        # We'll just animate theta_val shrinking
        new_theta = 15 * DEGREES
        
        # Update components
        new_p2 = circle.point_at_angle(new_theta)
        new_radial_line2 = Line(center, new_p2, color=WHITE, stroke_width=2)
        new_angle_arc = Arc(radius=0.5, start_angle=0, angle=new_theta, arc_center=center, color="#FF00FF")
        new_theta_label_pos = center + 0.8 * np.array([np.cos(new_theta/2), np.sin(new_theta/2), 0])

        self.play(
            Transform(radial_line2, new_radial_line2),
            Transform(angle_arc, new_angle_arc),
            theta_label.animate.move_to(new_theta_label_pos),
            state_point.animate.move_to(circle.point_at_angle(new_theta)),
            run_time=1.5
        )
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 4 ===
        self.lecture[2].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[3].set_color(WHITE) # Using White as requested in prompt "in white (#FFFFFF)"

        # Calculation display
        calc = MathTex(r"\text{Hits} = \frac{\pi}{\theta}", color=WHITE, font_size=32)
        self.place_at_grid(calc, "F3", scale_factor=1.0)
        
        self.play(Write(calc))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 5 ===
        self.lecture[3].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[4].set_color("#FFFFFF") # White

        # Highlight top half arc
        pi_arc = Arc(radius=2, start_angle=0, angle=PI, arc_center=center, color=WHITE, stroke_width=6)
        
        # We need a label for Pi radians
        pi_label = MathTex(r"\pi \text{ radians}", color=WHITE, font_size=28)
        self.place_at_grid(pi_label, "B3", scale_factor=1.0)

        self.play(Create(pi_arc), Write(pi_label))
        
        # Final point traversal to show it fits within Pi
        # Let's do a few more jumps along the Pi arc
        for i in range(2, 13): # 12 * 15 degrees = 180 degrees
            self.play(
                state_point.animate.move_to(circle.point_at_angle(i * new_theta)),
                run_time=0.2
            )

        self.wait(2)

class Section6Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        self.setup_layout(
            "Conclusion: The Final Tally", 
            [
                "Larger mass ratios create smaller, more precise angles.",
                "The collision count perfectly matches the digits of Pi.",
                "A surprising link between simple physics and mathematical constants."
            ]
        )
        
        # Colors
        yellow_color = "#FFFF00"
        white_color = "#FFFFFF"

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.lecture[0].set_color(yellow_color)
        
        # Block simulation visuals
        wall = Line(UP, DOWN, color=white_color).scale(2)
        self.place_at_grid(wall, "C1")
        
        block_m = Square(side_length=0.5, color=BLUE, fill_opacity=0.5)
        block_M = Square(side_length=1.0, color=RED, fill_opacity=0.5)
        
        self.place_at_grid(block_m, "C2")
        self.place_at_grid(block_M, "C3")
        
        counter_label = Text("Collisions:", font_size=24, color=white_color)
        counter_value = Text("3141", font_size=32, color=yellow_color)
        counter_group = VGroup(counter_label, counter_value).arrange(RIGHT, buff=0.3)
        self.place_at_grid(counter_group, "B3")
        
        self.play(
            FadeIn(wall),
            FadeIn(block_m),
            FadeIn(block_M),
            FadeIn(counter_group)
        )
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.lecture[0].set_color(white_color)
        self.lecture[1].set_color(yellow_color)
        
        # Table of mass ratios and counts
        table_header = Text("Mass Ratio | Bounces", font_size=20, color=white_color)
        table_row1 = Text("1 : 1          | 3", font_size=20, color=white_color)
        table_row2 = Text("1 : 100        | 31", font_size=20, color=white_color)
        table_row3 = Text("1 : 10,000     | 314", font_size=20, color=white_color)
        table_row4 = Text("1 : 1,000,000  | 3141", font_size=20, color=white_color)
        
        table = VGroup(table_header, table_row1, table_row2, table_row3, table_row4).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.place_in_area(table, "D2", "F5")
        
        self.play(Write(table))
        self.wait(2)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.lecture[1].set_color(white_color)
        self.lecture[2].set_color(yellow_color)
        
        # Fade out everything except collision counter value
        pi_text = Text("π ≈ 3.141...", font_size=48, color=yellow_color)
        self.place_at_grid(pi_text, "C3")
        
        self.play(
            FadeOut(wall),
            FadeOut(block_m),
            FadeOut(block_M),
            FadeOut(counter_label),
            FadeOut(table),
            ReplacementTransform(counter_value, pi_text)
        )
        
        self.wait(3)

outline.title: Mapping to Phase Space: The Velocity Vector
outline.content: Instead of watching the blocks move in space, we plot their velocities on a graph. Let the x-axis be the velocity of the big block (v1) and the y-axis be the velocity of the small block (v2). Every state of the system is just a single point on this graph.
outline.example: Show a 2D coordinate system where the 'state' point moves every time a collision occurs. A wall hit flips the y-coordinate; a block hit moves the point along a specific path.

storyboard.title: Mapping to Phase Space: The Velocity Vector
lecture_lines: We plot velocities on a two-dimensional graph.
Each point represents the current state of both blocks.
Collisions cause this state point to jump around.
animations: Create a 2D coordinate system with axes v1 (blue #0000FF) and v2 (green #00FF00), plus a yellow state point (#FFFF00).
Add a label 'System State' and the blocks icon [Asset: /scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/blocks.svg] next to the yellow point (#FFFF00) to show it represents both blocks.
Animate the yellow point (#FFFF00) jumping between positions, leaving a thin white trail (#FFFFFF) behind.

from manim import *
import numpy as np

class TeachingScene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text(line, font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (4x4 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                x = 0.5 + j * 1
                y = 2.2 - i * 1
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

    def place_in_area(self, mobject, top_left, bottom_right, scale_factor=1.0):
        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
        
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject

class Section3Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        self.setup_layout("Mapping to Phase Space: The Velocity Vector", [
            "We plot velocities on a two-dimensional graph.",
            "Each point represents the current state of both blocks.",
            "Collisions cause this state point to jump around."
        ])
        
        # Colors
        V1_COLOR = "#0000FF"
        V2_COLOR = "#00FF00"
        POINT_COLOR = "#FFFF00"
        TRAIL_COLOR = "#FFFFFF"
        HIGHLIGHT_COLOR = YELLOW

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.lecture[0].set_color(HIGHLIGHT_COLOR)
        
        # Create axes with colors specified in storyboard
        axes = Axes(
            x_range=[-2.2, 2.2, 1],
            y_range=[-2.2, 2.2, 1],
            x_length=4,
            y_length=4,
            axis_config={"include_tip": True},
            x_axis_config={"color": V1_COLOR},
            y_axis_config={"color": V2_COLOR}
        )
        x_label = MathTex("v_1", color=V1_COLOR).scale(0.8)
        y_label = MathTex("v_2", color=V2_COLOR).scale(0.8)
        
        # Positioning axes in area B2 to E5 (central part of the right side)
        self.place_in_area(axes, "B2", "E5")
        
        # Position labels near axes tips within 1 unit
        x_label.next_to(axes.x_axis.get_end(), DOWN, buff=0.1)
        y_label.next_to(axes.y_axis.get_end(), LEFT, buff=0.1)
        
        axes_group = VGroup(axes, x_label, y_label)
        self.play(Create(axes_group))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.lecture[0].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[1].set_color(HIGHLIGHT_COLOR)
        
        # Initial point at (v1_initial, 0). 
        v1_initial = -1.2
        v2_initial = 0
        point = Dot(axes.c2p(v1_initial, v2_initial), color=POINT_COLOR, radius=0.08)
        
        # The trail follows the point and uses #FFFFFF
        trail = TracedPath(point.get_center, stroke_color=TRAIL_COLOR, stroke_width=2)
        
        # State label that follows the point
        point_label = MathTex("(v_1, v_2)", color=POINT_COLOR).scale(0.7)
        point_label.next_to(point, UP, buff=0.1)
        
        # Keep label centered over the moving point
        point_label.add_updater(lambda d: d.next_to(point, UP, buff=0.1))

        self.add(trail)
        self.play(FadeIn(point), Write(point_label))
        self.wait(2)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.lecture[1].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[2].set_color(HIGHLIGHT_COLOR)
        
        # Physics logic for animation visualization (m1=5, m2=1)
        m1, m2 = 5.0, 1.0
        
        def get_next_velocities(v1, v2, type="block"):
            if type == "block":
                # Elastic collision: momentum and energy conservation
                v1_new = ((m1 - m2) / (m1 + m2)) * v1 + (2 * m2 / (m1 + m2)) * v2
                v2_new = (2 * m1 / (m1 + m2)) * v1 - ((m1 - m2) / (m1 + m2)) * v2
                return v1_new, v2_new
            else:
                # Wall hit: v2 flips sign (reflection across X-axis)
                return v1, -v2

        # Step 1: Blocks collide (moves along diagonal)
        v1_1, v2_1 = get_next_velocities(v1_initial, v2_initial, "block")
        self.play(point.animate.move_to(axes.c2p(v1_1, v2_1)), run_time=1.2, rate_func=linear)
        self.wait(0.3)
        
        # Step 2: Small block hits wall (instantly reflects across X-axis)
        v1_2, v2_2 = get_next_velocities(v1_1, v2_1, "wall")
        self.play(point.animate.move_to(axes.c2p(v1_2, v2_2)), run_time=0.6, rate_func=linear)
        self.wait(0.3)
        
        # Step 3: Blocks collide again
        v1_3, v2_3 = get_next_velocities(v1_2, v2_2, "block")
        self.play(point.animate.move_to(axes.c2p(v1_3, v2_3)), run_time=1.2, rate_func=linear)
        self.wait(0.3)

        # Step 4: Wall hit
        v1_4, v2_4 = get_next_velocities(v1_3, v2_3, "wall")
        self.play(point.animate.move_to(axes.c2p(v1_4, v2_4)), run_time=0.6, rate_func=linear)
        self.wait(1)
        
        # Clean up
        point_label.clear_updaters()
        self.play(FadeOut(point_label), self.lecture[2].animate.set_color(WHITE))
        self.wait(2)

outline.title: The Geometry of Energy: Stretching the Circle
outline.content: Explain that because Conservation of Energy (1/2 Mv1² + 1/2 mv2² = Constant) looks like the equation of an ellipse, we can 'rescale' the axes by the square root of the masses to turn that ellipse into a perfect circle.
outline.example: An animation showing a squashed oval (ellipse) being physically stretched vertically until it becomes a perfect, glowing circle. The 'state' of our blocks is now a point trapped on the rim of this circle.

storyboard.title: The Geometry of Energy: Stretching the Circle
lecture_lines: Energy conservation forms an elliptical path on our graph.
We rescale the axes to simplify the geometry.
The ellipse transforms into a perfect, uniform circle.
The system's state now moves along this circular boundary.
Geometry reveals hidden patterns in the block dynamics.
animations: Draw a green ellipse (#00FF00) centered at the origin of the velocity graph.
Display the scaling factors sqrt(M) and sqrt(m) in white (#FFFFFF) next to the axes.
Animate the green ellipse (#00FF00) stretching vertically until it becomes a perfect cyan circle (#00FFFF).
Add a bright cyan glow (#00FFFF) to the perimeter of the circle to highlight the state boundary.
Fade in a yellow Pi symbol (#FFFF00) at the center of the cyan circle.

from manim import *
import numpy as np

class TeachingScene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text(line, font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (4x4 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                x = 0.5 + j * 1
                y = 2.2 - i * 1
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

    def place_in_area(self, mobject, top_left, bottom_right, scale_factor=1.0):
        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
        
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject

class Section4Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        lecture_lines = [
            "Energy conservation forms an elliptical path on our graph.",
            "We rescale the axes to simplify the geometry.",
            "The ellipse transforms into a perfect, uniform circle.",
            "The system's state now moves along this circular boundary.",
            "Geometry reveals hidden patterns in the block dynamics."
        ]
        self.setup_layout("The Geometry of Energy: Stretching the Circle", lecture_lines)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.lecture[0].set_color(YELLOW)
        
        # Create coordinate axes for context
        # Using a coordinate system roughly centered in the right-side grid area
        axes = Axes(
            x_range=[-2, 2, 1],
            y_range=[-2, 2, 1],
            x_length=4.5,
            y_length=4.5,
            axis_config={"color": GREY_C},
            tips=False
        )
        self.place_in_area(axes, 'A1', 'F6')
        
        # Ellipse representing the initial energy equation (1/2 M v1^2 + 1/2 m v2^2 = Constant)
        ellipse = Ellipse(width=3.5, height=1.5, color="#00FF00")
        ellipse.move_to(axes.c2p(0, 0))
        
        v1_label = MathTex("v_1", font_size=24, color=WHITE)
        v2_label = MathTex("v_2", font_size=24, color=WHITE)
        self.place_at_grid(v1_label, 'C6', scale_factor=1.0)
        self.place_at_grid(v2_label, 'A3', scale_factor=1.0)
        
        self.play(Create(axes), Write(v1_label), Write(v2_label))
        self.play(Create(ellipse))
        self.wait(2)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.lecture[0].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[1].set_color(YELLOW)
        
        scaling_x = MathTex(r"\sqrt{M}", font_size=28, color="#00FF00")
        scaling_y = MathTex(r"\sqrt{m}", font_size=28, color="#00FF00")
        
        # Positioning scaling factors near the axes ends
        self.place_at_grid(scaling_x, 'D6', scale_factor=1.0)
        self.place_at_grid(scaling_y, 'A4', scale_factor=1.0)
        
        self.play(Write(scaling_x), Write(scaling_y))
        self.wait(2)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.lecture[1].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[2].set_color(YELLOW)
        
        # The transformation to a circle after rescaling the axes
        circle = Circle(radius=1.75, color="#00FFFF")
        circle.move_to(axes.c2p(0, 0))
        
        self.play(
            Transform(ellipse, circle),
            scaling_x.animate.set_color("#00FFFF"),
            scaling_y.animate.set_color("#00FFFF"),
            run_time=2
        )
        self.wait(2)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 4 ===
        self.lecture[2].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[3].set_color(YELLOW)
        
        # Highlight the perimeter with a glow effect
        # Using a VGroup of circles to simulate a glow
        glow = VGroup(*[
            Circle(radius=1.75 + i*0.05, color="#00FFFF", stroke_width=2).set_opacity(0.3 - i*0.05)
            for i in range(5)
        ])
        glow.move_to(axes.c2p(0, 0))
        
        # A small dot representing the state moving on the circle
        dot = Dot(color=WHITE).move_to(circle.point_from_proportion(0))
        
        self.play(FadeIn(glow))
        self.play(MoveAlongPath(dot, circle), run_time=3, rate_func=linear)
        self.play(FadeOut(dot))
        self.wait(2)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 5 ===
        self.lecture[3].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[4].set_color(YELLOW)
        
        # Fade in the symbol 'Pi' (#FFFF00) at the center of the circle
        pi_sym = MathTex(r"\pi", font_size=72, color="#FFFF00")
        self.place_in_area(pi_sym, 'C3', 'D4')
        
        self.play(FadeIn(pi_sym))
        self.wait(3)
        
        # Final state: reset lecture line color
        self.lecture[4].set_color(WHITE)
        self.wait(1)
